This page loads the run directory returned by [Run](run.qmd) and reads the
pad-to-ground capacitance. It needs only SCGSim, not Palace, so you can start
a new Python session.

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
- The returned run directory `.artifacts/SimplePad/pad-capacitance-01`.
- The `handoff_id` printed on the Prepare page.
:::

## Step 1: Load the result

```python
from scgsim.palace import resolve_palace_result

result = resolve_palace_result(
    ".artifacts/SimplePad/pad-capacitance-01",
    expected_handoff_id="<the handoff_id from Prepare>",
)
result.show_all_results()
```

If any output file is missing, or the directory belongs to another run,
`resolve_palace_result` stops with an error and does not return partial
numbers.

## Step 2: Read the capacitance

The report contains the capacitance matrix referenced to Ground. This model
has one terminal, so the matrix has a single entry, $C_{11}$: the pad-to-ground
capacitance. The same values are in `results/palace/terminal-C.csv` in the run
directory, in farads.

![Report output for this tutorial: the pad capacitance and its value at each
mesh refinement pass.](../../assets/simple-pad-capacitance.png){#fig-simple-pad-capacitance}

The earlier reference run gave $C_{11} \approx 95.4$ fF. Compare your model,
boundary and settings with that run, and review how $C_{11}$ changes across
adaptive passes. A large difference can reflect different vacuum padding or
Ground Net assignments.

::: {.callout-tip title="Record the setup with the number"}
A capacitance only has meaning together with its terminal and Ground choice.
Keep the run directory, or at least `config.json` and the report, next to the
value you use in a circuit model.
:::

The capacitance describes this geometry and this boundary choice. It is one
input to a circuit model, not a prediction of a qubit's spectrum.

## What changes the result

- **Boundary choice.** With `exterior_boundary_policy="ground"`, the outer
  vacuum boundary also becomes Ground. That adds capacitance to a distant
  enclosure. Choose it only if your device sits in a grounded box at that
  distance.
- **Vacuum size.** Too little padding pushes the field against the outer
  boundary and changes the value. Increase the padding until $C_{11}$ stops
  changing at the precision you need.
- **Mesh refinement.** Look at the per-pass history in the report. If
  $C_{11}$ is still changing between the last passes, raise `amr_max_passes`
  or tighten `amr_tolerance`.

Each change needs a new run directory: go back to [Prepare](prepare.qmd).
